input.quote: 14.2 Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
input.rationale: Section 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of Deliverables created specifically for Customer (per the § 1.4 definition, bespoke work product excluding Vendor Technology) and leaves Customer only a revocable, non-transferable licence expiring with the Order Form term. That contradicts our position that we own what we pay for. Sections 14.1 (Customer Data), 14.3 (Vendor Technology retained with the § 13.2 perpetual licence) and 14.4 (no joint ownership) are acceptable, so the minimal fix is to flip 14.2 to Customer ownership with an assignment from Vendor while preserving Vendor's retention of Vendor Technology under 14.3.

proposal.summary: Reverse Deliverable ownership to Customer with Vendor assignment; Vendor Technology remains with Vendor under 14.3
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We own the work product we pay for, so we have flipped ownership of Deliverables to Customer with an assignment from Vendor; Vendor Technology stays with Vendor under Section 14.3 and the Section 13.2 perpetual licence. A revocable, term-limited licence to our own bespoke deliverables is not acceptable; if Vendor cannot assign, our fallback is Vendor ownership plus a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable licence to use and modify the Deliverables.

ops.oldText: 14.2 Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
ops.newText: 14.2 Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer, and Vendor hereby irrevocably assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in each Deliverable upon creation. Vendor retains Vendor Technology in accordance with Section 14.3.
